words.definition: the creation of a genetically identical copy of a cell or organism
words.example: The debate focused on whether human cloning should ever be permitted.

words.definition: the deliberate alteration of an organism’s genetic material
words.example: Genetic modification can be used to produce crops with useful traits.

words.definition: having genetic material that has been deliberately altered by technology
words.example: The label states that the product contains genetically modified ingredients.

words.definition: the design or use of extremely small robotic devices at the nanoscale
words.example: Researchers hope nanorobotics could one day deliver medicine inside the body.

words.definition: a fertility treatment in which an egg is fertilised outside the body before being placed in the uterus
words.example: In vitro fertilisation has helped many people become parents.

words.definition: the attempt to choose the sex of a future child, usually through reproductive technology
words.example: Gender selection raises difficult ethical questions in some countries.

words.definition: the precise alteration, removal or replacement of DNA in a cell or organism
words.example: Gene editing may eventually help treat some inherited diseases.

words.definition: the use of living organisms, cells or biological processes to develop useful products or technologies
words.example: Biotechnology is widely used in medicine and agriculture.

words.definition: an artificial body part designed to replace a missing one
words.example: The runner uses an advanced prosthetic leg.

words.definition: a situation in which a choice must be made between competing moral principles
words.example: Editing human embryos creates an ethical dilemma for researchers.

words.definition: the direct manipulation of DNA to change the characteristics of an organism
words.example: Genetic engineering can introduce a desired trait into a crop.

words.definition: an organism in the early stages of development after fertilisation
words.example: Scientists discussed the rules governing research on human embryos.

words.definition: the natural ability to produce children or offspring
words.example: Age can affect fertility in both men and women.

words.definition: a hypothetical future point when artificial intelligence exceeds human intelligence and drives rapid technological change
words.japanese: 技術的特異点・シンギュラリティ
words.example: Some futurists believe the technological singularity could transform society.

words.definition: the introduction of a new idea, method or technology
words.japanese: 革新・イノベーション
words.example: Medical innovation has improved survival rates for many diseases.

words.definition: an unspecialised cell that can develop into other types of cell
words.example: Stem cells are studied for their potential in regenerative medicine.

words.definition: the average number of years a person in a particular population is expected to live
words.example: Improved healthcare has increased life expectancy in many countries.

words.definition: to completely eliminate a disease, problem or harmful condition
words.example: Vaccination programmes aim to eradicate certain infectious diseases.

words.definition: a being whose biological body is enhanced or supported by mechanical or electronic technology
words.example: The novel imagines a future in which humans become partly cyborg.

words.definition: the use of technology or medicine to improve human abilities beyond normal functioning
words.example: Human enhancement raises questions about fairness and access.

words.definition: a piece of equipment, especially an electronic tool, designed for a particular purpose
words.example: Most students carry at least one digital device every day.

words.definition: online platforms that allow users to create, share and interact with content and other people
words.example: Social media can connect people across long distances.

words.definition: excessive self-focus and admiration of one’s own appearance or abilities
words.japanese: 自己愛・ナルシシズム
words.example: Some critics link constant self-promotion online with narcissism.

words.definition: the act of working together to achieve a shared goal
words.example: Online tools make international collaboration easier.

words.definition: the ability to understand and share another person’s feelings
words.example: Face-to-face conversation can help develop empathy.

words.definition: an informal exchange of ideas or information between people
words.example: The teacher asked students to put away their phones during conversation.

words.definition: able to communicate or interact with others, especially through technology
words.example: Messaging apps keep families connected across countries.

words.definition: the act of ignoring someone in person in order to pay attention to a phone
words.japanese: スマホを優先して相手を無視すること
words.example: Phubbing can make people feel ignored during a meal.

words.definition: driving while attention is diverted by a phone or another activity
words.japanese: ながら運転・注意散漫運転
words.example: Texting is a dangerous form of distracted driving.

words.definition: the amount of time spent using devices with screens
words.example: Parents often set limits on children’s screen time.

words.definition: compulsive and harmful dependence on digital devices, games or online services
words.example: The article examines signs of digital addiction among teenagers.

words.definition: the right or ability to keep personal information and activities from unwanted access
words.example: Users should check the privacy settings on social media accounts.

words.definition: the record of information and activity a person leaves through their use of the internet
words.japanese: デジタルフットプリント
words.example: Old posts can remain part of a person’s digital footprint for years.

words.definition: the state of being separated from other people or lacking social contact
words.example: Heavy internet use does not always prevent feelings of isolation.

words.definition: communication or contact that creates genuine understanding, connection or value
words.example: The project encourages meaningful interaction between generations.

words.definition: attempting to perform several tasks or activities at the same time
words.example: Multitasking can reduce concentration when studying.

words.definition: a set of rules or instructions used by a computer to solve a problem or make a decision
words.example: The platform’s algorithm decides which posts appear first.

words.definition: an environment where people mainly encounter opinions that reinforce their existing views
words.example: Social media can create an echo chamber around political opinions.

words.definition: a healthy and balanced relationship with digital technology
words.japanese: デジタル・ウェルビーイング
words.example: Turning off notifications can improve digital wellbeing.

words.definition: communication or social contact that takes place through the internet
words.example: Online interaction can be useful but may lack non-verbal cues.

words.definition: a particular method or skill used to produce a desired artistic effect
words.example: The artist developed a new technique for layering paint.

words.definition: the purpose or aim behind an action or creative work
words.example: Understanding the artist’s intention changed how I viewed the piece.

words.definition: related to ideas of beauty, style or artistic appearance
words.example: The building combines practical design with aesthetic appeal.

words.definition: an explanation or understanding of the meaning of a work, event or idea
words.example: Different viewers may have different interpretations of the same artwork.

words.definition: the circumstances and background that help explain the meaning of something
words.example: The political context is important for understanding the painting.

words.definition: the state or identity of being the creator of a work
words.japanese: 作者性・著作者であること
words.example: Digital collaboration can make authorship difficult to define.

words.definition: to display an object or work publicly, especially in a gallery or museum
words.example: The museum will exhibit the sculpture next month.

words.definition: to select, organise and present works or materials for an exhibition or collection
words.japanese: 企画・選定して展示する
words.example: She was invited to curate an exhibition of digital art.

words.definition: the quality of being new, distinctive and not copied from others
words.example: The judges praised the originality of the student’s design.

words.definition: the ability to produce new and imaginative ideas or works
words.example: Technology can support creativity as well as efficiency.

words.definition: belonging to or characteristic of the present time
words.example: The gallery specialises in contemporary art.

words.definition: different from what is usual, traditional or expected
words.japanese: 型破りな・慣例にとらわれない
words.example: The artist uses unconventional materials such as recycled plastic.

words.definition: the communication of ideas, emotions or experiences through art
words.example: Music became an important form of artistic expression for him.

words.definition: the material, form or method used by an artist to create a work
words.example: Photography is the artist’s preferred medium.

words.definition: a large artistic work arranged in a specific space, often using multiple materials
words.japanese: インスタレーション作品
words.example: Visitors can walk through the interactive installation.

words.definition: widely recognised and strongly associated with a particular person, style or period
words.japanese: 象徴的な・非常に有名な
words.example: The photograph became an iconic image of the movement.

words.definition: the analysis and evaluation of the qualities, meaning or value of a work
words.example: The film received both praise and criticism from reviewers.

words.definition: to recognise and understand the value, quality or significance of something
words.japanese: 価値を理解する・鑑賞する
words.example: Studying the context helped students appreciate the artwork more fully.

words.definition: a copy or reproduction of another person’s style, action or work
words.example: The artist argues that imitation can still involve creativity.

words.definition: the quality of being new, unusual or different from what is familiar
words.example: The initial novelty of the technology attracted large crowds.
